gwas_catalog.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog
gwas_catalog.notes: Use for curated genome-wide association signals and trait/locus validation. GWAS loci are usually small-effect and ancestry/model dependent.

clinvar.name: NCBI ClinVar
clinvar.conflict_of_interest: Public NIH variant archive with external submitter classifications
clinvar.notes: Use for clinical variant classification. Always check current review status, submitter conflicts, and clinical assertion date.

clingen.name: ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity and Actionability
clingen.conflict_of_interest: NIH-funded clinical genetics resource; expert panel curation
clingen.notes: Use for clinical gene-disease validity, actionability, and expert-panel interpretation frameworks.

genereviews.name: GeneReviews
genereviews.notes: Use for monogenic disease clinical context, inheritance, testing limits, and management overview.

cpic.name: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC)
cpic.notes: Use only for how to interpret already-available PGx results. Does not mean raw DNA is sufficient for medication changes.

pharmgkb.name: PharmGKB
pharmgkb.notes: Use for drug-gene annotations and PGx evidence summaries. Clinical use still requires guideline and clinician context.

omim.name: OMIM
omim.notes: Use for rare monogenic disorder context. Consumer raw SNP data usually cannot rule in or rule out these conditions.

gnomad.name: gnomAD
gnomad.notes: Use for allele frequency and rare-variant plausibility checks. Frequency alone does not classify pathogenicity.

cdc_mthfr.name: CDC MTHFR and Folic Acid Guidance
cdc_mthfr.notes: Use to prevent common MTHFR overclaims; genotype does not mean folic acid cannot be processed.

pmdd_review.name: PMDD neuroactive steroid sensitivity review
pmdd_review.conflict_of_interest: None declared in accessible article metadata; verify article disclosures when using clinically
pmdd_review.notes: Use for PMDD framing as hormone-sensitivity/neurosteroid/GABA-related biology, not as a single-SNP diagnosis.

hpo.name: Human Phenotype Ontology
hpo.notes: Use to standardize symptom prompts and phenotype tags.

acog_premenstrual_disorders.name: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Premenstrual Disorders
acog_premenstrual_disorders.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society guideline; review the guideline disclosures when using clinically
acog_premenstrual_disorders.notes: Use for PMS/PMDD assessment and treatment framing. The app must not turn a marker or a report into a diagnosis or treatment plan.

womenshealth_pmdd.name: Office on Women's Health: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
womenshealth_pmdd.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services public health resource
womenshealth_pmdd.notes: Use for plain-language symptom timing, symptom diaries, and emergency mental-health safety wording.

acog_premenstrual_syndrome.name: ACOG: Premenstrual Syndrome
acog_premenstrual_syndrome.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society patient guidance; review current clinical advice when using clinically
acog_premenstrual_syndrome.notes: Use for practical PMS nutrition, activity, sleep, relaxation, and supplement-caution prompts. Keep recommendations individualized and do not turn them into genotype-specific treatment.

womenshealth_pms.name: Office on Women's Health: Premenstrual Syndrome
womenshealth_pms.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services public health resource
womenshealth_pms.notes: Use for plain-language food, activity, sleep, stress, and symptom-support prompts. Individual response and clinical context remain more important than a DNA association.

acog_combined_contraception.name: ACOG: Combined Hormonal Birth Control
acog_combined_contraception.notes: Use to distinguish combined estrogen-plus-progestin methods from progestin-only methods and to require exact product identification.

acog_progestin_only_contraception.name: ACOG: Progestin-Only Hormonal Birth Control
acog_progestin_only_contraception.notes: Use the term progestin for synthetic progesterone-like contraceptive ingredients and do not infer a medication class from DNA.

cdc_usmec_2024.name: CDC U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 2024
cdc_usmec_2024.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention public-health guidance
cdc_usmec_2024.notes: Use for thrombophilia and contraceptive-method safety context. The app must not use a raw SNP call to choose, stop, or change contraception, and routine population screening is not implied.

nice_adenomyosis_heavy_bleeding.name: NICE NG88: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding Assessment and Management
nice_adenomyosis_heavy_bleeding.conflict_of_interest: UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline
nice_adenomyosis_heavy_bleeding.notes: Use for suspected adenomyosis symptom triage and imaging prompts; transvaginal ultrasound is preferred when clinically appropriate.

medlineplus_adenomyosis.name: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia: Adenomyosis
medlineplus_adenomyosis.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Library of Medicine public health resource
medlineplus_adenomyosis.notes: Use for symptom and diagnostic-limit language. Do not imply that a raw DNA file confirms or excludes adenomyosis.

menstrual_cycle_physiology.name: NCBI Bookshelf: Physiology, Menstrual Cycle
menstrual_cycle_physiology.conflict_of_interest: NCBI Bookshelf medical reference; verify current clinical guidance for patient care
menstrual_cycle_physiology.notes: Use to explain that the late-luteal transition is characterized by withdrawal/fall of estradiol and progesterone in a natural cycle, not a presumed estrogen spike.

acog_dysmenorrhea_painful_periods.name: ACOG: Dysmenorrhea and Painful Periods
acog_dysmenorrhea_painful_periods.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society patient guidance; review current clinical advice when using clinically
acog_dysmenorrhea_painful_periods.notes: Use for symptom timing, primary versus secondary period pain, evaluation prompts, and general supportive options. Do not convert painful-period symptoms or DNA into a diagnosis or medication plan.

acog_chronic_pelvic_pain.name: ACOG: Chronic Pelvic Pain
acog_chronic_pelvic_pain.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society patient guidance; review current clinical advice when using clinically
acog_chronic_pelvic_pain.notes: Use for escalation questions involving worsening or persistent pelvic pain, bowel/bladder symptoms, bleeding, fever, pregnancy possibility, and urgent warning signs.

nice_menstrual_related_migraine.name: NICE CG150: Headaches and Menstrual-Related Migraine
nice_menstrual_related_migraine.conflict_of_interest: UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guideline; review current prescribing advice when using clinically
nice_menstrual_related_migraine.notes: Use for headache-diary timing, menstrual-related migraine assessment, medication-overuse awareness, aura differentiation, and pregnancy/contraception safety prompts. Do not provide drug doses or select treatment from DNA.

cdc_migraine_contraception_safety.name: CDC U.S. MEC 2024: Migraine and Contraceptive Method Classification
cdc_migraine_contraception_safety.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention public-health guidance
cdc_migraine_contraception_safety.notes: Use to prompt clinician review of migraine type, especially aura, and the exact contraceptive method. The app must not infer migraine type or contraception safety from raw DNA.

acog_preconception_counseling.name: ACOG: Prepregnancy Counseling
acog_preconception_counseling.conflict_of_interest: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists committee opinion developed with the American Society for Reproductive Medicine; review disclosures when using clinically
acog_preconception_counseling.notes: Use for explicit preconception context, medication and supplement review, chronic-condition optimization, family/genetic history, nutrition, activity, substance, and safety screening. Do not infer pregnancy intent, anatomy, identity, or fertility from DNA.

cdc_planning_for_pregnancy.name: CDC: Planning for Pregnancy
cdc_planning_for_pregnancy.evidence_type: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention public-health guidance
cdc_planning_for_pregnancy.notes: Use for plain-language preconception prompts, including medical history and review of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, supplements, and vitamins.

asrm_fertility_evaluation_women_2021.name: ASRM: Fertility Evaluation of Infertile Women
asrm_fertility_evaluation_women_2021.evidence_type: American Society for Reproductive Medicine committee opinion
asrm_fertility_evaluation_women_2021.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society guidance; review the document disclosures when using clinically
asrm_fertility_evaluation_women_2021.notes: Use for clinician-directed fertility evaluation. Tests must be interpreted in the full clinical context; do not convert consumer SNPs into ovarian-reserve, ovulation, or fertility predictions.

aua_asrm_male_infertility_2024.name: AUA/ASRM: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men
aua_asrm_male_infertility_2024.evidence_type: American Urological Association/American Society for Reproductive Medicine clinical guideline
aua_asrm_male_infertility_2024.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society guideline; AUA index identifies the guideline as amended in 2024; review current document disclosures
aua_asrm_male_infertility_2024.notes: Use for concurrent partner evaluation, semen-analysis and male-factor clinical context, and fertility-preserving medication review. Do not infer sperm quality, fertility, or treatment suitability from consumer SNPs.

dietary_guidelines_2025_2030.name: Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025-2030
dietary_guidelines_2025_2030.notes: Use as general dietary-pattern baseline. Individual medical, allergy, religious/cultural and lab-confirmed requirements override general guidance.

usda_fooddata_central.name: USDA FoodData Central
usda_fooddata_central.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Department of Agriculture public data resource; data sources vary by food type
usda_fooddata_central.notes: Use for exact nutrient values and food lookup. This JSON stack stores rule tags, not full nutrient composition tables.

fda_major_food_allergens.name: FDA Food Allergies and Major Food Allergens
fda_major_food_allergens.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Food and Drug Administration public regulatory resource
fda_major_food_allergens.notes: Use for U.S. major food allergen categories; sesame is included through the FASTER Act implementation. Allergy diagnosis still requires clinical context.

usda_big_9_allergens.name: USDA FSIS Big 9 Allergens
usda_big_9_allergens.notes: Use for consumer-facing Big 9 allergen wording: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans and sesame.

nih_ods_omega3.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Omega-3 Fact Sheet
nih_ods_omega3.notes: Use for ALA/EPA/DHA distinctions, fish/algal sources and omega-3 supplement caveats.

nih_ods_selenium.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Selenium Fact Sheet
nih_ods_selenium.notes: Use for selenium food sources, Brazil-nut variability, upper-limit and toxicity guardrails.

nih_ods_magnesium.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Magnesium Fact Sheet
nih_ods_magnesium.evidence_type: NIH nutrient and medication-interaction fact sheet
nih_ods_magnesium.notes: Use for food-first magnesium context, supplemental upper-limit framing, kidney caution, and medication interactions.

nih_ods_iron.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Iron Fact Sheet
nih_ods_iron.notes: Use for iron food/supplement context and deficiency/excess assessment; genotype does not replace iron studies.

nih_ods_folate.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Folate Fact Sheet
nih_ods_folate.notes: Use for folate/folic acid intake context and lab interpretation with one-carbon metabolism markers.

cdc_mthfr_folic_acid.name: CDC MTHFR and Folic Acid Guidance
cdc_mthfr_folic_acid.notes: Use to prevent MTHFR overclaims and false folic-acid avoidance recommendations.

nih_ods_b12.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Vitamin B12 Fact Sheet
nih_ods_b12.notes: Use for B12 food sources, deficiency risk and supplement/fortified food context.

nih_ods_vitamin_b6.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Vitamin B6 Fact Sheet
nih_ods_vitamin_b6.evidence_type: NIH nutrient and supplement safety fact sheet
nih_ods_vitamin_b6.notes: Use for vitamin B6 food sources, supplement upper-limit framing, neuropathy risk from excessive intake, and medication interactions; do not convert a symptom pattern or genotype into a B6 dose.

nih_ods_choline.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Choline Fact Sheet
nih_ods_choline.notes: Use for choline adequate intake, food sources, pregnancy context and deficiency/excess caveats.

nih_ods_vitamin_d.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Vitamin D Fact Sheet
nih_ods_vitamin_d.notes: Use for vitamin D intake/lab context; genotype does not diagnose deficiency.

fda_pharmacogenomic_biomarkers.name: FDA Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers in Drug Labeling
fda_pharmacogenomic_biomarkers.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulatory resource
fda_pharmacogenomic_biomarkers.notes: Use only for drug-label-supported biomarker context. Raw array results do not justify medication changes; review the current label and clinician/pharmacist guidance.

fda_pharmacogenetic_associations.name: FDA Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations
fda_pharmacogenetic_associations.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulatory resource
fda_pharmacogenetic_associations.notes: Use to separate therapeutic-management recommendations from pharmacokinetic-only or potential-response associations. Patients should not adjust medication without a prescriber.

cpic_guidelines.name: CPIC Pharmacogenomic Guidelines
cpic_guidelines.conflict_of_interest: Professional guideline consortium; review individual guideline disclosures
cpic_guidelines.notes: Use to interpret an available validated PGx phenotype for a drug; CPIC guidance is not a reason to infer a phenotype from an incomplete consumer SNP panel.

cpic_clopidogrel_2022.name: CPIC: CYP2C19 and Clopidogrel Guideline (2022 Update)
cpic_clopidogrel_2022.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_clopidogrel_2022.notes: Use for validated clinical CYP2C19 phenotype interpretation when clopidogrel antiplatelet therapy is being considered. A consumer-array SNP is not a complete phenotype and must not drive self-directed medication changes.

cpic_warfarin.name: CPIC: Warfarin Based on CYP2C9, VKORC1 and CYP4F2
cpic_warfarin.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline resource; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_warfarin.notes: Use for the current CPIC warfarin guideline pathway. INR, indication, age, interacting medicines, diet, and clinical monitoring remain necessary; raw consumer-array data cannot determine a warfarin dose.

cpic_statins_2022.name: CPIC: SLCO1B1, ABCG2 and CYP2C9 Statin Guideline (2022)
cpic_statins_2022.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_statins_2022.notes: Use for validated clinical PGx context around statin-associated musculoskeletal symptoms. It does not authorize a raw consumer-array result to stop, select, or dose a statin.

cpic_opioids_2020.name: CPIC: CYP2D6 and Opioids Guideline
cpic_opioids_2020.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_opioids_2020.notes: Use for validated CYP2D6 phenotype context for codeine and tramadol pain treatment. The guideline does not make one consumer SNP a complete metabolizer result.

cpic_tamoxifen_2018.name: CPIC: CYP2D6 and Tamoxifen Guideline
cpic_tamoxifen_2018.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_tamoxifen_2018.notes: Use for validated CYP2D6 phenotype and medication-interaction review in tamoxifen care. Oncology decisions must account for cancer context and other therapies; raw DNA cannot direct endocrine-treatment changes.

cpic_ssri_2023.name: CPIC: CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2B6 and Serotonin-Reuptake Antidepressants (2023)
cpic_ssri_2023.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_ssri_2023.notes: Use for validated clinical PGx context when an antidepressant question is active. A consumer-array finding cannot independently select, stop, or change a psychiatric medication.

cpic_cyp2c9_nsaids_2020.name: CPIC: CYP2C9 and Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs Guideline
cpic_cyp2c9_nsaids_2020.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_cyp2c9_nsaids_2020.notes: Use for validated clinical CYP2C9 diplotype/phenotype context with selected NSAIDs. The guideline supports exposure-related clinical discussion but does not make a consumer-array result a diagnosis of intolerance or a self-directed medication instruction.

cpic_cyp3a5_tacrolimus_2015.name: CPIC: CYP3A5 Genotype and Tacrolimus Dosing Guideline
cpic_cyp3a5_tacrolimus_2015.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_cyp3a5_tacrolimus_2015.notes: Use only for validated clinical CYP3A5 interpretation in active tacrolimus care, with transplant-team oversight and therapeutic-drug monitoring. Consumer-array data cannot determine a tacrolimus dose.

cpic_nat2_hydralazine_2025.name: CPIC: NAT2 Genotype and Hydralazine Therapy Guideline
cpic_nat2_hydralazine_2025.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_nat2_hydralazine_2025.notes: Use for validated clinical NAT2 diplotype/phenotype context during hydralazine care. Consumer-array markers cannot independently assign phenotype or direct a dose or medication change.

cpic_cyp2c19_ppi_2020.name: CPIC: CYP2C19 and Proton Pump Inhibitor Guideline
cpic_cyp2c19_ppi_2020.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_cyp2c19_ppi_2020.notes: Use for first-generation PPI and dexlansoprazole exposure/response context; the guideline makes no recommendation for esomeprazole or rabeprazole and a complete CYP2C19 phenotype is required.

cpic_cyp2b6_efavirenz_2019.name: CPIC: CYP2B6 and Efavirenz Guideline
cpic_cyp2b6_efavirenz_2019.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_cyp2b6_efavirenz_2019.notes: Use for CYP2B6 phenotype, efavirenz exposure, and CNS-adverse-effect context in clinical HIV care; raw single-SNP calls do not assign a complete phenotype or dose.

cpic_cyp2c9_hla_phenytoin_2020.name: CPIC: CYP2C9/HLA-B and Phenytoin Guideline
cpic_cyp2c9_hla_phenytoin_2020.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_cyp2c9_hla_phenytoin_2020.notes: Use for phenytoin narrow-therapeutic-index, CYP2C9 exposure, and HLA-B*15:02 severe cutaneous-reaction context; validated clinical genotype/phenotype and monitoring are required.

nih_ods_supplements.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements Fact Sheets
nih_ods_supplements.evidence_type: NIH dietary supplement safety and nutrient resource
nih_ods_supplements.notes: Use for nutrient forms, upper limits, medication interactions, deficiency/excess context and pregnancy/lactation cautions before presenting supplement ideas.

aha_physical_activity_warning_signs.name: American Heart Association Physical Activity Warning Signs
aha_physical_activity_warning_signs.conflict_of_interest: American Heart Association public health resource
aha_physical_activity_warning_signs.notes: Use for stop-and-escalate symptoms during activity, including chest discomfort, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, and fast or uneven heartbeat.

cdc_activity_stop_signs.name: CDC National Diabetes Prevention Program Activity Safety Signs
cdc_activity_stop_signs.notes: Use as a general activity safety guardrail; raw DNA never clears a user to ignore symptoms.

cdc_prediabetes_lifestyle.name: CDC National Diabetes Prevention Program Lifestyle Change Program
cdc_prediabetes_lifestyle.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention public-health guidance
cdc_prediabetes_lifestyle.notes: Use for general healthy-eating, physical-activity, sleep, stress, and weight-management support when diabetes risk is clinically relevant. Do not turn a common SNP into a diagnosis or prescribe a program from DNA alone.

niddk_prediabetes_tests.name: NIDDK Recommended Tests for Identifying Prediabetes
niddk_prediabetes_tests.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases public-health resource
niddk_prediabetes_tests.notes: Use to frame A1C, fasting plasma glucose, and oral glucose tolerance testing as clinical tests interpreted with patient context; genotype does not diagnose prediabetes or diabetes.

niddk_fatty_liver_diagnosis.name: NIDDK Diagnosis of NAFLD/NASH
niddk_fatty_liver_diagnosis.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases public-health resource
niddk_fatty_liver_diagnosis.notes: Use for history, blood-test, imaging, and differential-diagnosis boundaries around fatty-liver evaluation; a PNPLA3 or TM6SF2 marker is not a diagnosis.

aha_dyslipidemia_2026.name: AHA 2026 Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia
aha_dyslipidemia_2026.conflict_of_interest: American Heart Association professional guidance; review the guideline disclosures when using clinically
aha_dyslipidemia_2026.notes: Use for measured lipid risk assessment, at-least-once-in-adulthood Lp(a) measurement, selective ApoB use, and clinician-guided treatment decisions. Do not use raw DNA to prescribe or stop therapy.

gene_reviews_hemochromatosis.name: GeneReviews: HFE-Related Hemochromatosis
gene_reviews_hemochromatosis.notes: Use for incomplete penetrance, sex/life-stage differences, and iron-study context. A common HFE result is not a diagnosis and does not establish iron excess.

nih_caffeine_general_context.name: FDA Consumer Caffeine Guidance
nih_caffeine_general_context.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Food and Drug Administration public health resource
nih_caffeine_general_context.notes: Use for general caffeine context and the need to account for individual sensitivity, health conditions, medicines, and pregnancy; do not convert a CYP1A2 signal into a fixed personal limit.

endocrine_testosterone_hypogonadism.name: Endocrine Society Testosterone Therapy Guideline Resources
endocrine_testosterone_hypogonadism.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society guideline; review the guideline disclosures when using clinically
endocrine_testosterone_hypogonadism.notes: Use for the boundary that suspected testosterone deficiency requires compatible symptoms plus consistently low, accurately measured testosterone, usually confirmed with repeat morning testing. Do not screen or prescribe from raw DNA.

endocrine_gender_affirming_hormone_thera.name: Endocrine Society: Gender Dysphoria/Gender Incongruence Guideline Resources
endocrine_gender_affirming_hormone_thera.conflict_of_interest: Professional medical society guideline; review the guideline disclosures when using clinically
endocrine_gender_affirming_hormone_thera.notes: Use for clinician-directed hormone therapy, regular clinical evaluation, hormone-level monitoring, fertility counseling, and long-term safety follow-up. DNA cannot determine an individual regimen or response.

acog_transgender_gender_diverse_care.name: ACOG: Health Care for Transgender and Gender Diverse Individuals
acog_transgender_gender_diverse_care.conflict_of_interest: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists clinical guidance; review the guidance disclosures when using clinically
acog_transgender_gender_diverse_care.notes: Use for respectful, goal-directed hormone-care context, product-specific monitoring, and avoiding assumptions about identity, anatomy, fertility, or hormone response.

acog_optimizing_postpartum_care.name: ACOG: Optimizing Postpartum Care
acog_optimizing_postpartum_care.conflict_of_interest: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists clinical guidance; review the guidance disclosures when using clinically
acog_optimizing_postpartum_care.notes: Use for ongoing, individualized postpartum care, follow-up timing, recovery, contraception, mental health, and chronic-condition review.

acog_breastfeeding_medication_support.name: ACOG: Optimizing Support for Breastfeeding as Part of Obstetric Practice
acog_breastfeeding_medication_support.conflict_of_interest: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists clinical guidance; review the guidance disclosures when using clinically
acog_breastfeeding_medication_support.notes: Use for individualized feeding support and medication review; a medically indicated medication is not automatically a reason to stop breastfeeding.

acog_urgent_maternal_warning_signs.name: ACOG: Urgent Maternal Warning Signs
acog_urgent_maternal_warning_signs.conflict_of_interest: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists patient-safety resource
acog_urgent_maternal_warning_signs.notes: Use for urgent symptoms during or after pregnancy and the instruction to tell emergency clinicians about a current or recent pregnancy.

cdc_medicine_pregnancy.name: CDC: Medicine and Pregnancy
cdc_medicine_pregnancy.evidence_type: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention public-health guidance
cdc_medicine_pregnancy.notes: Use for reviewing every medicine with a healthcare provider during pregnancy and for directing users to drug-specific FDA information.

ncbi_lactmed.name: NCBI: Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed)
ncbi_lactmed.evidence_type: National Library of Medicine evidence database
ncbi_lactmed.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Library of Medicine public evidence resource
ncbi_lactmed.notes: Use for substance-specific information on breast-milk and infant levels, reported infant effects, and possible alternatives; review current records with a clinician.

medlineplus_testicle_pain.name: MedlinePlus: Testicle Pain
medlineplus_testicle_pain.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Library of Medicine public health resource
medlineplus_testicle_pain.notes: Use for urgent symptom escalation: sudden severe testicle pain needs immediate medical care. This is a symptom-safety rule, not a genetic inference.

niddk_thyroid_tests.name: NIDDK: Thyroid Tests
niddk_thyroid_tests.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases public health resource
niddk_thyroid_tests.notes: Use for the boundary that thyroid status is evaluated with clinical blood tests such as TSH and free T4, with additional tests or imaging when indicated; do not use common SNPs to diagnose thyroid disease or direct treatment.

nhlbi_sleep_apnea_diagnosis.name: NHLBI: Sleep Apnea Diagnosis
nhlbi_sleep_apnea_diagnosis.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute public health resource
nhlbi_sleep_apnea_diagnosis.notes: Use for symptom prompts, sleep diaries, and sleep-study follow-up when snoring, witnessed apneas, gasping, or daytime sleepiness warrant evaluation; chronotype SNPs do not diagnose sleep apnea.

aaaai_food_allergy_diagnosis.name: AAAAI: Food Allergy Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment
aaaai_food_allergy_diagnosis.conflict_of_interest: American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology professional education resource
aaaai_food_allergy_diagnosis.notes: Use for exposure-linked history, allergist-directed testing, and urgent anaphylaxis escalation. Do not infer food allergy from AOC1/HNMT or immune SNPs, and do not recommend unsupervised elimination or food challenges.

nih_ods_iodine.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Iodine Fact Sheet
nih_ods_iodine.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_iodine.notes: Use for iodine food/supplement safety and the risk of excessive intake; do not convert thyroid-pathway SNPs into iodine dosing advice.

nih_ods_vitamin_a.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin A and Carotenoids Fact Sheet
nih_ods_vitamin_a.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_vitamin_a.notes: Use for preformed vitamin A versus provitamin A distinctions, excess-intake risks, and medication interactions; do not convert a common marker into a vitamin-A dose.

nih_ods_pregnancy_supplements.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Dietary Supplements and Life Stages—Pregnancy
nih_ods_pregnancy_supplements.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_pregnancy_supplements.notes: Use for pregnancy and preconception supplement context, especially the distinction between preformed vitamin A and provitamin A carotenoids.

nih_ods_zinc.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Zinc Fact Sheet
nih_ods_zinc.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_zinc.notes: Use for zinc upper-intake, copper-depletion, and medication-interaction context; do not use SLC30A8 or SLC39A8 markers to prescribe zinc.

nih_ods_potassium.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Potassium Fact Sheet
nih_ods_potassium.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_potassium.notes: Use for kidney function, serum potassium, salt-substitute, and ACE/ARB or potassium-sparing-diuretic safety context; do not turn a common marker into potassium advice.

nih_ods_calcium.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Calcium Fact Sheet
nih_ods_calcium.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_calcium.notes: Use for calcium upper-intake, kidney-stone, and medication-interaction context; do not use VDR, CASR, CYP24A1, or SLC34A1 markers to prescribe calcium.

nih_ods_vitamin_k.name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements: Vitamin K Fact Sheet
nih_ods_vitamin_k.conflict_of_interest: U.S. National Institutes of Health public health resource
nih_ods_vitamin_k.notes: Use for consistent vitamin-K intake and warfarin interaction context; do not use VKORC1/CYP2C9/CYP4F2 raw-array data to set anticoagulant dosing.

cpic_dpyd_fluoropyrimidines.name: CPIC: DPYD and Fluoropyrimidine Guideline
cpic_dpyd_fluoropyrimidines.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_dpyd_fluoropyrimidines.notes: Use for clinical DPYD genotype-to-fluoropyrimidine interpretation. Consumer-array observations require validated clinical confirmation and oncology review.

fda_dpyd_fluoropyrimidine_safety.name: FDA: DPD Deficiency Safety Labeling for Fluorouracil
fda_dpyd_fluoropyrimidine_safety.conflict_of_interest: U.S. Food and Drug Administration regulatory resource
fda_dpyd_fluoropyrimidine_safety.notes: Use for fluorouracil DPD/DPYD safety-label context; do not turn a raw SNP into a treatment or dose instruction.

cpic_thiopurines_2025.name: CPIC: TPMT and NUDT15 Thiopurine Guideline (2025 Update)
cpic_thiopurines_2025.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_thiopurines_2025.notes: Use for clinical TPMT/NUDT15 phenotype and thiopurine starting-dose context. The guideline is for clinicians and does not make a consumer SNP a standalone prescription.

cpic_hla_abacavir.name: CPIC: HLA-B*57:01 and Abacavir Guideline
cpic_hla_abacavir.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_hla_abacavir.notes: Use for drug-specific HLA-B*57:01 clinical testing and abacavir safety; raw SNP proxies are not equivalent to clinical HLA typing.

cpic_hla_carbamazepine.name: CPIC: HLA-B/HLA-A and Carbamazepine/Oxcarbazepine Guideline
cpic_hla_carbamazepine.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_hla_carbamazepine.notes: Use for HLA-B*15:02, HLA-A*31:01, and carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine clinical testing context, including severe cutaneous adverse-reaction boundaries.

cpic_hla_allopurinol.name: CPIC: HLA-B*58:01 and Allopurinol Guideline
cpic_hla_allopurinol.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_hla_allopurinol.notes: Use for HLA-B*58:01 and allopurinol severe cutaneous adverse-reaction clinical context; raw SNP proxies require confirmation.

cpic_g6pd.name: CPIC: G6PD and Medication Guideline
cpic_g6pd.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_g6pd.notes: Use for drug-specific G6PD risk classification and the need to account for genotype, enzyme phenotype, medication, and concurrent illness.

cpic_ryr1_cacna1s_anesthesia.name: CPIC: RYR1/CACNA1S and Volatile Anesthetics/Succinylcholine
cpic_ryr1_cacna1s_anesthesia.conflict_of_interest: Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline; review current guideline disclosures
cpic_ryr1_cacna1s_anesthesia.notes: Use for validated RYR1/CACNA1S susceptibility interpretation and anesthesia-team communication; consumer-array findings cannot independently clear risk.

gene_reviews_malignant_hyperthermia.name: GeneReviews: Nonsyndromic Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility
gene_reviews_malignant_hyperthermia.notes: Use for RYR1/CACNA1S testing limits, inheritance, and clinical susceptibility boundaries.

ncbi_pseudocholinesterase.name: NCBI Bookshelf: Biochemistry, Pseudocholinesterase
ncbi_pseudocholinesterase.notes: Use for inherited and acquired pseudocholinesterase deficiency, succinylcholine/mivacurium exposure, dibucaine testing, and clinical confirmation limits.

ncbi_ugt1a1_irinotecan.name: NCBI Bookshelf: Irinotecan Therapy and UGT1A1 Genotype
ncbi_ugt1a1_irinotecan.notes: Use for UGT1A1/irinotecan toxicity context and the distinction between a clinical UGT1A1 result and a consumer-array proxy.

user_declared_values_required.name: DNA Tools support policy: user-declared values required
user_declared_values_required.conflict_of_interest: Project safety contract; not an external clinical source
user_declared_values_required.notes: Used when a recommendation depends on a value the DNA file cannot provide, such as current medication, diet, allergy, pregnancy/lactation, or personal goal.

clinical_confirmation_required.name: DNA Tools support policy: clinical confirmation required
clinical_confirmation_required.conflict_of_interest: Project safety contract; not an external clinical source
clinical_confirmation_required.notes: Used to prevent a raw-array observation from being presented as a diagnosis, treatment instruction, or medication change.

phenotype_required.name: DNA Tools support policy: phenotype required
phenotype_required.conflict_of_interest: Project safety contract; not an external clinical source
phenotype_required.notes: Used when symptoms, timing, exposure, family history, or other observed phenotype is required to interpret a genetic signal.

lab_confirmation_required.name: DNA Tools support policy: laboratory confirmation required
lab_confirmation_required.conflict_of_interest: Project safety contract; not an external clinical source
lab_confirmation_required.notes: Used when an actionable question depends on a laboratory result rather than genotype alone.

safety_guardrail.name: DNA Tools support policy: safety guardrail
safety_guardrail.conflict_of_interest: Project safety contract; not an external clinical source
safety_guardrail.notes: Used for stop, avoid, escalation, interaction, and uncertainty language that must remain visible even when the genetic signal is weak or incomplete.
